name: The Thule migration
traveler: The Thule people, ancestors of the Inuit
summary: Whale hunters of the Bering Strait, with umiaks, dog sledges and harpoons, move east along the Arctic coast in a few generations, across Canada to Greenland. They displace or absorb the Dorset people and meet the Norse in Greenland. Every Inuit community from Alaska to Greenland descends from them.

stops.note: Thule culture grows on both sides of the strait, hunting bowhead whales from skin boats.
East along the Arctic coast in the warm centuries, when the whales range farther.
